questions.q: Where should the diagonal strap of a seatbelt pass?
options: Under the arm
Across the neck only
Over the collarbone, across the middle of the shoulder
Behind the back
questions.explain: A strap that passes under the arm or behind the back won’t stop the body correctly in a crash, and may cause injury itself.

questions.q: Who must wear a seatbelt in the car?
options: Only in the front seats
Only the driver and the passenger beside them
Only passengers over 18
The driver and every passenger, in the front seats and rear seats alike
questions.explain: Regulation 83B requires the driver and all passengers, in every seat in the car, to wear a belt or be secured in a suitable seat.

questions.q: Why must a pregnant passenger not remove her seatbelt “to protect the baby”?
options: Because there’s no risk to the baby in a crash at all
Because the best way to protect the baby is to keep the mother correctly belted
Because it’s always forbidden without exception, even in a stationary car
Because the belt replaces a doctor’s check-up
questions.explain: The lap strap passes under the bump, across the hips; if the mother isn’t belted, both she and the baby are injured far more in a sudden stop or crash.

questions.q: A driver is reversing in a car park. Is he exempt from wearing a seatbelt at that moment?
options: No, a seatbelt is compulsory in every situation, without exception
Only if the car park is private
Yes, reversing is one of the exceptions the law recognises
Only in an automatic car
questions.explain: Regulation 83C exempts from wearing a belt while reversing - this is a specific exception, not a general exemption.

questions.q: What does the seatbelt pretensioner do?
options: Tightens the strap instantly at the moment of impact, before the body has time to move
Applies the brakes automatically
Inflates the airbag
Loosens the strap to make it more comfortable
questions.explain: The seatbelt pretensioner shortens the distance the body travels forward, improving the protection the belt gives.

questions.q: Up to what age must a child travel in a child safety seat with its back facing the front of the car?
options: {{fact:child.safety_seat_age}}
{{fact:child.booster_age_max}}
{{fact:child.rear_facing_age}}
14 years
questions.explain: Up to age {{fact:child.rear_facing_age|n}}, a rear-facing seat is required, to spread the force of impact across the child’s whole back (reg. 83A(c)).

questions.q: From age 3 up to what age is it permitted to carry a child in a booster seat instead of a full child safety seat?
options: 12 years
5 years
{{fact:child.rear_facing_age}}
{{fact:child.booster_age_max}}
questions.explain: From age {{fact:child.safety_seat_age|n}} up to age {{fact:child.booster_age_max|n}}, a suitable child safety seat or booster seat is permitted (reg. 83A(b)(2)).

questions.q: Why must a child not be seated in a rear-facing child safety seat, facing an active airbag?
options: Because an airbag that deploys forcefully can badly injure the child instead of protecting them
Because the airbag simply won’t deploy at all if there’s a child seat
Because it only causes a warning light
Because it only breaches the manufacturer’s terms, with no real danger
questions.explain: Regulation 83A(d) requires disconnecting an active airbag facing a child safety seat or booster seat, for exactly this reason.

questions.q: What is the advantage of ISOFIX anchoring over installing a child safety seat with a belt?
options: It removes the need for harness straps
It reduces the price of the seat
Installation is more stable and easier, without depending on tensioning the car’s belt
It’s only meant for children over 8
questions.explain: ISOFIX anchors the seat directly to metal anchor points in the car, so installation is more stable and less dependent on human error.

questions.q: What is the simple test that a child safety seat’s harness straps are correctly tightened?
options: There’s no way to check this at home
A whole hand fits comfortably under the strap
One finger barely fits under the strap
The strap comes loose easily when pulled
questions.explain: A correctly tightened strap leaves room for only one finger - no more.

questions.q: Parents are carrying a 5-year-old in the car. What does the law require?
options: A regular seatbelt only, with no extra seat
A rear-facing seat only
No special requirement beyond age 3
A suitable child safety seat or booster seat matched to their height and weight
questions.explain: A 5-year-old is in the range between {{fact:child.safety_seat_age}} and {{fact:child.booster_age_max}}, so a suitable child safety seat or booster seat is required.

questions.q: Why is a child in greater danger than an adult when left alone in a closed, hot car?
options: This is only true on especially hot summer days
There’s no real extra danger, it’s just a misconception
The child will always be asleep and won’t feel anything
Their body heats up faster and they find it harder to regulate the heat
questions.explain: A small child’s body heats up faster than an adult’s and struggles more to regulate heat, so the danger is high even on a relatively mild day.

questions.q: What is the most effective protection against forgetting a child in the car?
options: A fixed habit - leaving something essential in the back seat so you have to look back every time you get out
Relying on memory each time
Leaving a window cracked open
Listening to the radio to stay alert
questions.explain: Most cases aren’t deliberate neglect but a disrupted routine - a fixed habit protects better than relying on memory.

questions.q: What is the legal severity of leaving a child up to age {{fact:child.alone_max_age|n}} without proper supervision, in a way that endangers their life?
options: An administrative offence carrying only a licence suspension
Not an offence at all if the time is short
A serious criminal offence carrying imprisonment (Penal Law, section 361)
Only a fine, with no points
questions.explain: Section 361 of the Penal Law sets imprisonment of up to three years, and an additional year if it was done negligently.

questions.q: You see a child alone in a car parked in the sun, visibly distressed, doors locked. What do you do?
options: Look for the parent nearby for half an hour before calling for help
Photograph the car and leave
Call the police or Magen David Adom immediately and act to get the child out without waiting, even if you need to break a window
Wait by the car for the parent to return, in case they’re nearby
questions.explain: In a situation of distress, every minute counts - call {{fact:emergency.police}} or {{fact:emergency.mda}} immediately and act, don’t wait or search alone.

questions.q: Why isn’t a window cracked open enough to protect a child left in the car?
options: It’s enough for a short time of up to 10 minutes
A window cracked open is actually more dangerous than a closed one
The temperature in the cabin still rises very quickly, even with the crack open
It’s enough if the car is parked in the shade
questions.explain: Even with a window cracked open and even in the shade, the temperature in the cabin rises too fast for it to be safe to leave a child alone.

questions.q: Why must an airbag work together with a seatbelt, and not instead of it?
options: Without a belt, the body reaches the airbag at the wrong angle and speed, and may be injured by it
Because the belt inflates the airbag faster
There’s no connection between the two - each works separately
Because the airbag isn’t meant to protect the head at all
questions.explain: The airbag is designed to complete the action of the belt, not replace it.

questions.q: What does an airbag warning light that stays on, and doesn’t go off after starting the engine, signal?
options: The airbag is in an even better ready state than usual
It signals that the tyres need air
A fault in the airbag system - get to a garage
It’s normal and can be ignored
questions.explain: An airbag light that stays on permanently signals a fault - the airbag may not deploy in a crash, or may deploy when it shouldn’t.

questions.q: What is the correct height for a headrest?
options: As low as possible, so it doesn’t block the view backward
Significantly higher than the head, with no limit
Any height, it’s only for comfort
Its top level with the crown of the head at least, as close to the head as possible
questions.explain: A headrest that’s too low doesn’t support the head in a rear-end collision and can increase whiplash.

questions.q: Why is a correctly adjusted headrest important in a rear-end collision?
options: It supports the head early and reduces sharp whiplash of the neck
It only affects seating comfort
It replaces the need for a seatbelt
It completely prevents any injury in a crash
questions.explain: In a rear-end collision the body is pushed forward while the head lags behind for a moment; a headrest that is close and high enough supports the head sooner.

questions.q: When must an active airbag in the front passenger seat be disconnected?
options: When a child is seated there in a child safety seat or booster seat
On every drive, even with an adult passenger
Only on trips longer than an hour
Never - it’s forbidden by law
questions.explain: Regulation 83A(d) requires disconnecting an active airbag facing a child’s safety seat or booster seat.

questions.q: Why is an unsecured heavy object on the back seat dangerous in a crash?
options: It keeps moving forward at the speed of travel and can injure the passengers in front of it
It can only scratch the upholstery
It slows the car down and helps braking
There’s no risk if the object is relatively light
questions.explain: An unsecured object keeps moving at the speed of the car, like any free body in a crash - so even a relatively light object can cause harm.

questions.q: What is the correct way to carry a dog in the car?
options: On the driver’s lap while driving
Loose in the cabin, so it feels comfortable
Tied with a regular adult seatbelt only
In a suitable safety harness, a secured carrier, or the boot behind a separating net
questions.explain: A dog loose in the car is a danger to itself and the passengers, and a serious distraction to the driver; it must be carried secured.

questions.q: From which side do you let a child out of and into the car on the street?
options: From the road side, to save time
From any side, as long as you hurry
From the side nearest the pavement, once the car has come to a complete stop
While driving very slowly
questions.explain: Getting in or out from the road side exposes the child to traffic; wait until the car stops completely and let them out from the pavement side.

questions.q: Heavy cargo in a private car - where does it correctly belong?
options: On the back seat, unsecured
In the boot, tied down or in a cargo net
Between the driver’s feet, for easy access
On the parcel shelf, under the rear windscreen
questions.explain: Cargo on the parcel shelf both blocks the view through the rear-view mirror and becomes a projectile in a sudden stop.
